name: Albert Daniels
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember recognizing a stranger behind me as somebody I wanted to tell.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Albert asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I am the client waiting behind her. I heard myself offer a story I have never told our own tailor.
appearance: Albert has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Albert rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Albert talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Albert's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To give the widow the choice of hearing the stranger's story.
family: Dane Aubin is Albert’s cousin. Albert chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Dane brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Two portions*, Dane says, “I take the stairs because the bell is louder than the tenant can bear.”
connections: Hollis Bowen. An old school fitting helps the next customer find words for an unrelated garment memory.

reactions.response: Albert asks the tailor and widow what access others would lose if the mirror moved.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Albert tells the stranger when the next opening is, then stays with the neighbor until their turn comes.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Albert says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
